mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of six consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both personal savings (RSAFS) and unemployment (UNRATE) over three months, while consumption (GDPC1) stagnates, signals a savings glut and weak demand, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and UNRATE rise while GDPC1 is flat over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when RSAFS and UNRATE rise while GDPC1 is flat for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp cut in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month, in response to a financial shock, signals an emergency easing that boosts liquidity and supports S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops >0.5% in one month due to emergency action
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) following an emergency FEDFUNDS cut >0.5% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during four consecutive months of PAYEMS above its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a broad-based recovery in demand and supply, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both > 12-month MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both HOUST and INDPRO are above their 12-month MA for three consecutive months.
